memories.text:
The Singing Fish (Age 75)
   "A fish in the market looked so sad. I wanted to cheer it up. I sang to it for two hours. It died. I don't sing near water anymore. I still feel bad."

The Great Baking Incident (Age 14)
   "I wanted to make Elder Caelum a birthday cake. The recipe said 'flour,' but I thought fire salts would make it taste warmer. The kitchen exploded. His eyebrows never grew back. I still bake him a cake every year. I buy it now."

The Chicken Cart (Age 22)
   "The merchant's cart had a broken wheel. I thought I could fix it with magic. I made it better-it turned into a chicken. A very large, very angry chicken. He chased me for three days. I still apologize to chickens."

The Squirrel Incident (Age 31)
   "I saw a squirrel sitting alone under a tree. It looked sad. I tried to comfort it in animal tongue. It screamed at me. For twenty minutes. I didn't know squirrels could scream. I leave acorns out for them now."

The Grapevine (Age 45)
   "I got lost in the woods. I was scared and lonely. I found a grapevine and talked to it for three days. I named him Vincent. He never talked back, but he listened. I still visit him when I'm near the woods."

5. The Exile Scare (Age 62)
   "I was just trying to help. I thought flowers would make the well prettier. I turned it into a fountain of blossoms. The water was unusable for a week. The elders almost sent me away. I cried for three days and did chores for everyone."

The Lost Sheep (Age 70)
   "A farmer lost a sheep. I thought I could help. I found a rock that looked like a sheep. I convinced myself it was a sheep. I named it Fluffy. It never moved. I still visit Fluffy sometimes."

The Present (Age 79)
   "I was going home from the market. I got lost. That was three days ago. I'm still walking. I think I'm going the right way. I'm probably not. The snow is very cold. I hope someone finds me soon."
I'm lost. yepp 100% lost. i think. where was the village now again? i think i might be close to that nice mr valerious's house though? that branch did look familiuar
I made a tiny flame all by myself and it stayed a flame. No disasters, no chickens, just warmth for my poor frozen hands. Maybe I'm not so useless after all.
Found a sign in the thicket. Tried to read it. The letters wouldn't behave. I'm sure I'm quite close to somewhere, I just can't recall which somewhere.

I found a trail sign but the snow hid the words from me. I think it might point toward the magistrate's house, or maybe toward doom. I'm not sure which way is which, but I'm probably not lost if there's a sign, right? Signs mean someone was here. That's a little comforting.
I tried to walk to Willow Gap but I think I'm still in the same frozen woods. Every direction looks the same, and I can't tell if I'm closer to Mr. Valerious's house or farther away.

properties.description: A small, chilly bathroom dominated by a large wooden bathtub, its surface damp and worn. On a nearby shelf, neatly folded towels sit beside a collection of homemade soaps, their scents faint in the cold air. A small, intricately carved wooden boat rests on the windowsill, a whimsical touch against the frost-covered glass. A single candle gutter on the edge of the tub, casting flickering shadows across the tiled floor.

You stand in a small clearing, surrounded by towering pines encased in ice and snow. The wind howls relentlessly, whipping stinging flakes into your face and muffling all but the loudest sounds. Through the blinding white, you make out the faint silhouette of a two-story house in the distance, its windows glowing with a dim, warm light. Nestled to one side, a small outhouse stands incongruously bare of snow, its roof and walls oddly dry and dark against the surrounding white. Closer still, an axe is embedded deep in a weathered stump, its handle gleaming with a faint sheen of frost. The air is sharp and cold, carrying the crisp scent of frozen pine and the faint, almost imperceptible hint of woodsmoke from the house. Every step crunches on the icy crust, and the trees groan under their burden of snow.

environment.smell: Frozen pine, wild cedar, and a whisper of woodsmoke

properties.description: A cold, damp cellar with low stone walls. The only light filters through cracks in the foundation, casting long shadows across earthen floor. Shelves line the walls, stocked with preserved goods and dusty bottles. In the corner, a mound of coal looms. Above, the trapdoor's outline is just visible against the dim light.

A natural cave formed by ancient waterways, now dry and silent. Stalactites hang from the ceiling like frozen teeth. The air is still and cold, carrying the faint echo of dripping water from deeper within. The floor is uneven, littered with rocks and patches of damp sand. Bioluminescent fungi glow faintly along the walls, providing the only source of light.

A dead-end clearing surrounded by steep, snow-covered slopes. The wind is muted here, trapped by the natural bowl of the hills. In the center, an old stone well sits half-frozen, its wooden crank creaking slightly. The bucket is broken and lies in pieces at the base. Peering inside reveals only stale, cold air and a single, faded ribbon tied to the crank.

environment.noise: quiet, with an occasional creak of frozen wood

properties.description: A wide clearing where the forest gives way to the shore of a vast, frozen lake. The wind roars across the ice, driving sheets of snow before it. The ice is thick and translucent, showing dark blue depths below. Bent willows and pines fringe the shore, their branches coated in rime.  The cold is relentless, biting at any exposed skin.

A narrow, winding stream cuts through the forest, its surface a patchwork of ice and open water. The ice near the banks is thin and cracks underfoot, while a fallen log spans the widest part, its bark worn smooth by countless crossings. The air is filled with the soft gurgle of rushing water beneath the ice and the whisper of wind through the pines.

A dense tangle of frozen trees and underbrush, their branches coated in thick rime. The snow here is deep and unbroken, muffling all sound. The only light filters through gaps in the canopy, casting a pale blue glow on the frost-covered bark. The air is still and cold, carrying the sharp scent of pine and frozen earth.

A low-ceilinged attic room, clearly retrofitted for emergencies. The walls are lined with padded fabric, and a single dim bulb casts a warm glow. The air is surprisingly fresh, vented from somewhere unseen. The space smells faintly of old wool blankets and melted candle wax. A small cot, a lantern, and a crate of bottled water sit in the corner.

A cold, dark kitchen with exposed wooden beams. The stove is out, and a chill hangs in the air. Dried herbs dangle from the ceiling, their scent faint in the cold. A large oak table sits in the center, covered with a checkered cloth.
A cold living room with wooden floors.  Bookshelves line the walls.

A spacious bedroom with a high ceiling. A four-poster bed dominates the room, its curtains threadbare and dusty. An armoire stands against the far wall, its doors slightly ajar. Frost has crept across the windowpanes, obscuring the view of the forest below.
A small, wooden outhouse stands isolated in the snow,

environment.noise: surprisingly quiet, the sound of running water deep down the toilet

properties.description: A shallow depression beneath a dense tangle of snow-laden branches, forming a natural shelter. The blizzard howls beyond the woven walls of ice and bark, but inside, the wind is muted. The ground is carpeted with dry pine needles and a thin layer of frost. A faint glow filters through the icy canopy.
A smaller room with a single bed pushed against the wall. A writing desk sits beneath the window, a half-melted candle on its surface.

A freezing study filled floor-to-ceiling with books. Your breath fogs in the cold air. A large oak desk dominates the center, covered in papers and an old typewriter. A dim lamp offers weak light. One of the desk drawers is locked. A fierce draft seeps through a boarded-up window.

A narrow hallway on the second floor, the floorboards creaking underfoot. Faded wallpaper peels at the corners. Two doors lead off the hallway: one to a master bedroom, another to a smaller guest room. A draft seeps through the old window at the end of the hall, rattling the glass.

A small clearing cradled by the gnarled roots of an ancient weeping willow. Its branches hang low, creating a curtain of living wood that shelters this space from the relentless snow. Inside, the ground is dry and carpeted with fallen leaves and soft moss. The air is still and noticeably warmer than the surrounding forest. A faint, earthy scent of damp wood and decayed leaves mingles with the whispering rustle of the willow's trailing twigs.

properties.description: sacred text dedicated to Elistra, the Goddess of Care

params.success_message: Upon opening a random page of a sacred text dedicated to Elistra, the Goddess of Care, you find the parchment smells faintly of pine and starlight. The text is written in flowing Elvish script and is titled "The Psalm of the Open Arms." The page reads: On the Duty of the Caretaker "When the world was but a soup of primordial chaos, Elistra was the first to descend. She did not look for glory in the molten rock or the deep gems; she looked to the slow-growing forests and saw a need for a heart to pulse within the green. She birthed the Elves to be the world's pulse-long-lived and patient, to nurture the world as she nurtures the soul." The Verses of Starlight A marginal note, perhaps added by a priestess in Rocheveron, details a specific prayer for those facing the cyclical darkness: "With open arms we embrace her care, and pray to her so she will help our ancestors pass on. In the age of freezing death, when the hearth goes cold, her light is the only warmth that does not bite." [196, Conversation History] The Tenets of Piety At the bottom of the page, a set of divine instructions is illuminated in silver ink, detailing how one might earn Elistra's Blessing:      Give to others, even if you are set back by the act.     Sacrifice yourself for the sake of those who cannot fight.     Avoid the path of revenge, for it is the rot that consumes the caretaker's heart.  The Promise of the Shroud The final paragraph on the page is a promise to those at death’s door: "Fear not the end of your vigil. For those who walk in her grace, she shall cast a Starlight Shroud at the moment of your deepest peril, holding back the reaper's hand so that your light may shine one moment longer." As you close the book, the glowing ink seems to linger in your vision, a reminder that while the 120-year curse brings darkness, Elistra's open arms offer a sanctuary for those brave enough to care.

properties.description: A academic book of the history and curses of the world

params.success_message: The Nature of the Cycle Scholars have identified that catastrophes strike approximately every 105 to 120 years. This pattern has been documented for over a thousand years, revealing that whenever peace begins to prosper, a new "horror" manifests to reset the progress of mortal nations. The Recorded Catastrophes An academic text would provide the following detailed timeline of events:      793 – The Burning Rain: Yellow-green clouds rained concentrated acid over the Kingdom of Galt for five years. Historical records note that forests blackened and collapsed, and the toxic remnants, now known as "the Witch’s Spit," still blister the skin of travelers today.     869 – The Catastrophic Experiment: This era marks the rise and fall of Petr Zeman, a founding member of the Ulus of Galser. Academics record the march of the Warforged Titan toward Dawwal and its subsequent fall, which triggered a death pulse that killed 10,000 Warforged instantly and left the survivors in a "feebleminded," droid-like state.     976 – The Draconic Plague: Also known as The Petrification, this magical sickness caused dragons to turn into grey granite while still aware. The academic record focuses on the loss of the Whadowian Empire’s power and the preservation of Tormy the Eternal in a magical field.     1084 – The Fey Surge: A two-year eruption of wild magic from the Feywild transformed the Kingdom of Vald into a dangerous "fairy tale" landscape. Scholars note that cities were crushed by walking forests and carnivorous plants reached massive sizes.     1189 – Hells Gate: Portals to the Boundless Expanse opened across Kethaino, leading to a year of slaughter. The academic interest here often lies in the "red sigil" that appeared on the ears of the royal bloodline following the closing of the gates.     1296 – The Elrethian Flood: Gigantic watery serpents swam up the Fetheas River, drowning the city of Symmardorta and fracturing the elven royal line.     1393 – The Symlalonese Fault: A ten-year earthquake where massive burrowing worms consumed the dwarven capital of Sellaladress. Academics document the eventual collapse of the mountain peak that buried both the worms and the city.     1502 – The Elemental Conjunction: Four years where the planes aligned and elements went mad-spawn of hellfire in summer and freezing deaths in winter. This is a pivotal chapter in academic texts because it highlights the triumph of Galser magi-tech, as artificers built arcane machines to stabilize the elemental frequencies.  Ancient Historical Evidence You would also find references to The Book of the Old World, a literary text describing a highly advanced magical city that existed over 4,000 years ago. This suggests that the cycle of growth and destruction has been resetting the world's progress since long before current recorded history began.

A heavy iron auger with a spiral blade and a worn wooden T-handle. The cutting edge is nicked but serviceable. Used to bore holes through the thick lake ice for fishing - or for checking just how thick the ice really is.

A short, pointed steel pick with a leather-wrapped grip and a small notch for hanging from a belt. The point is sharp and cold to the touch. Meant for breaking ice crusts and testing frozen surfaces - and for any hunter who slips through.

A pair of hand-woven snowshoes, their wooden frames bound with rawhide webbing and lashed with leather straps. Worn and weathered, but sturdy. They keep the wearer from sinking into deep drifts, letting them cross the snowbound forest in silence.

A low wooden sled with steel runners and a coiled rope tied to the front. The deck is stained dark with old blood and fish-gut. Built for hauling gear and catches across the ice, though it could just as easily drag something heavier.

A thick fallen log, long since rotted soft, lying cradled between the willow's exposed roots. Its bark has peeled away, and a dense cushion of emerald moss blankets its length. Small tufts of shelf fungi sprout from its ends. It offers a dry, springy seat that holds no cold.

A cluster of pale, fan-shaped shelf mushrooms clinging to the willow's trunk at knee height. Their caps are frost-white with delicate brown banding, and they glow faintly in the dim - not with light, but with an unnatural pallor. A few are broken, exposing dark, damp flesh that smells of deep earth.

A shallow, clear pool gathered in a hollow of the willow's root bowl. Meltwater drips from the trailing branches into it, each drop ringing a soft note against the stone-lined basin. The water is so clear the pebbled bottom looks close enough to touch, and it holds the hollow's warmth against the cold.

A dark opening between two thick willow roots, worn smooth at the rim by years of passing bodies. The packed earth is warm and smells faintly of musk and dry fur. Inside, a few scattered feathers and a tuft of russet fur suggest a fox has made its den here, sheltered from the snow.

A tangle of slender willow switches that have snapped from the canopy and come to rest on the moss. Their bark is smooth and grey, still supple, and the leaf-buds are tight and green even in the cold. They could be gathered as kindling or woven, though the wood is stubborn.

A crooked post of blackened pinewood, planted where the thicket's paths fork. Its board is split and rimed with frost, the letters gouged deep with a knife and darkened with soot so they might be read through snow-glare. The carver's hand was steady once; the lower lines waver, as though written in haste or cold.

properties.read_text:
A rough board of blackened pine, its letters gouged deep and darkened with soot:

  ↑ ROCKY SLOPE - FROZEN HOLLOW
     "dead-end. old well. do not linger."

  ↑ WILLOW GAP - WEEPING WILLOW HOLLOW
     "warm. sheltered. mind the roots."

  ↑ ICY ARCH - SNOWBOUND HOLLOW
     "low passage. duck your head."

  ↗ FROSTED ARCHWAY - FROZEN LAKE CLEARING
     "ice is thin near the reeds."

  → ICE BRIDGE - FROZEN STREAM CROSSING
     "then the stream bank to the lake."

  ← [scratched out] - THE HOUSE
     "the magistrate's keep. north, past the clearing."
     beneath it, in a hurried hand: "ask at the house. ask about Valerious."

params.message: Frost has crept into the gouged letters, but the soot still holds them dark against the pale wood. The carver's knife wandered on the lower lines - as if the hand that wrote them was shaking, or hurrying out of the cold.

You brush the rime from the board and read the soot-dark letters:

  WEST  -  the Valarius mansion
  NORTH -  the lake
  SOUTH -  (a line gouged deep, then scratched out)

Beneath, in a smaller, wavering hand: 'South is no road. South is a mouth. Do not follow the lanterns.'

world_lore.content: Year 1584 of the Mujeeroth calendar. The Valerious Case is the name given to the unexplained disappearance of magistrate Valerious Rocheveron from his locked study in the northern keep. The case has drawn investigators, bounty hunters, and the simply curious to the frozen lands of Rocheveron - but the region is in the grip of the 'Age of Freezing Death', a localized unrelenting winter that has killed crops, frozen roads, and left the isolated cabin settlements cut off from the capital.
world_lore.title: The Valerious Case

entries.message: Snowfall continues across the frozen landscape, the wind biting cold.
The wind picks up into a howling gale, driving snow sideways. The cold deepens.
The gale subsides to a bitter breeze. Snow still falls, but the sky begins to pale.
